issue.title: test_streaming_transfer_succeeds_while_progress_continues times out in the full lane but passes serially

task_type_fields.evidence: Observed at HEAD 812ddbc3aed901f77385830432216598f8843e4c in ToolRun 9284154363a11646773177b11c5098b4: git operation test.clone stalled after 0.15s without progress. The full governed test lane ended 4 failed, 60208 passed, 18 skipped; the other failures have independent baseline witnesses. The exact node passed serially on the unchanged implementation tree (0.33s call), with no edits to the streaming test or implementation. Observed rate: one failure in one full-lane run, zero failures in one serial rerun. The test launches a Python child that flushes progress every 0.05s, with a 0.15s stall deadline; the underlying scheduler or state interaction is not yet established. Duplicate search and recent-task sweep found no report for this node; no causally related active epic found. Full failure and serial-pass evidence are attached.

issue.creation_reason: The standard agent check failed on an unchanged streaming test during continuation finalizer implementation. A focused unchanged-tree rerun passed, so this timing failure needs independent diagnosis.

evidence.note: Relayed proposal from sase-1rq.2.1.4.1.3 note #4 and survival inventory .2 note #3: the same node failed with SddGitCommandTimeout in full contention repeat jc6gbkn1bdjd. Current src/sase/sdd/_git_runner.py checks the stall clock before draining readable stderr; a starved reader can false-timeout with progress buffered. 4a7ce0f330 changed the test child to sh and the window to 0.5s; production ordering remains. This is a mechanism lead for the existing node-specific report, not proof of fail/pass under matched conditions. Also routing to active publication-drain epic sase-1nf.10.1, whose phase .2 changed streaming cancellation.
